body:
> The platform would guarantee that the auto generated ids are unique within the ShadowDOM realm (including outside any ShadowDOM). There's no need to make them unique between two different realms as far as I know.

@bahrus Could you expand on what you mean by this? The parenthetical makes it confusing.

---

I'll also link back to my two comments: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10143#issuecomment-2209641481 and https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10143#issuecomment-3207672419.

The key point I want to highlight is that my original suggestion is tied to ["template instantiation"](https://github.com/WICG/webcomponents/blob/gh-pages/proposals/Template-Instantiation.md) and the new syntax is part of the ["declarative DOM parts"](https://github.com/WICG/webcomponents/blob/gh-pages/proposals/DOM-Parts-Declarative-Template.md) proposal.

Yes, during the latest round of DOM parts discussions, all the vendors were strongly considering (maybe still are) adjusting the server [rendered html before it becomes part of the DOM tree](https://eisenbergeffect.medium.com/the-future-of-native-html-templating-and-data-binding-5f3e52fda259) based on the presence of a "parseparts" attribute.  That tells me that this proposal should be feasible.

Usually (always?), id's within the root document should be unique.  The root document is what I mean by outside any ShadowDOM realm.  One of the great things about ShadowDOM is the id's only need to be unique within that document fragment, without stepping on the toes of any other ShadowDOM'd custom elements.  Not sure if that can help reduce the size of the id's a bit and allow for more parallel processing, but wanted to say it, at the risk of causing confusion which I guess I did 🙂.
Updated based on @mayank99 's feedback and other thoughts.

One thing that jumped out to me in the responses to my questions is that so many mention repeated content from components, and even templates specifically: https://notes.igalia.com/XlsPwU5sQfuaWYHwhtBMtA

I really like the idea of making this a feature of templates. I especially like that it uses only existing mechanisms for the actual element associations, and thus doesn't require any additional plumbing in the browser engine beyond the logic to generate unique IDs as necessary.

One comment does mention "Random UUIDs not being ideal in static site generation as every page would be different in every build, making selective syncing of _actually_ changed pages to storage impossible." It seems implied from your respective examples, but it might be good to consider an explicit goal of speccing the ID generation such that the same input always generates the same output.

@alice Great point about deterministic output. It doesn't have to be random. If we're looking at prior art, the two frameworks cited (React and Vue) do already produce a stable unique ID which is based on position in the DOM. Beyond static site generation, having stable IDs is also a requirement for "hydration" — the ID produced declaratively and imperatively for the same element should always match.
I've incorporated @alice 's helpful feedback, let me know if I missed anything.

> **alice** Great point about deterministic output. It doesn't have to be random. If we're looking at prior art, the two frameworks cited (React and Vue) do already produce a stable unique ID which is based on position in the DOM. Beyond static site generation, having stable IDs is also a requirement for "hydration" — the ID produced declaratively and imperatively for the same element should always match.

react and vue's `useId` is **NOT** unique based on position in the DOM... they are incremental, so calling useId again and again will produce different id's. and based in which order an input are created might also change. 

Something I did was to hash the outerHTML of an input (and sometimes also the label) to create a deterministic random id. 
(good for when you want to share a deep link or store the unsaved data)

```js
/** @param {string} str */
function hash (str) {
  let hash = 2166136261
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    hash ^= str.charCodeAt(i)
    hash = (hash * 16777619) >>> 0
  }
  return 'el-' + hash.toString(36)
}

// Exempel
label.for = input.id = hash(input.outerHTML) // ex: "el-1gk5r2"
```

Good enough for my usecase to always be deterministic "random" every time. the order of which the arguments matters here as well when using outerHTML...

some consideration: 
- Bad if the attribute (like `value`) change all the time
- Alternative use something like xPath (but again: bad if the DOM location is different all the time)
- Could combine the attributes of `input.form`, or the index of where the element is located in `input.form.elements`

---

Another thing is why do inputs and label really need to have uniq ids?
why haven't we done the same thing that have been done for commands
```js
const popover = document.getElementById('mypopover')
const toggleBtn = document.getElementById('toggleBtn')
toggleBtn.commandForElement = popover
```
⬇️ 
```js
const label = document.querySelector('label')
const input = document.querySelector('input')
label.forElement = input
```

> > If we're looking at prior art, the two frameworks cited (React and Vue) do already produce a stable unique ID which is based on position in the DOM.
> 
> react and vue's `useId` is **NOT** unique based on position in the DOM... they are incremental, so calling useId again and again will produce different id's. and based in which order an input are created might also change.

I shouldn't have said DOM position; these frameworks generate an ID before anything even gets rendered to the DOM. But it very much does depend on position in the component tree (i.e. _virtual_ DOM). Here's a writeup from one of the maintainers of Preact: https://www.jovidecroock.com/blog/preact-use-id/. That it produces new IDs upon subsequent calls is a secondary mechanism (in addition to the position-based ID) which is useful in cases like when you need multiple IDs within the same component.
 
Ultimately these are just implementation details (which can change at any time). What's more important to highlight is that these IDs are stable across builds and across environments.

> Another thing is why do inputs and label really need to have uniq ids? why haven't we done the same thing that have been done for commands

That's a separate issue. https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11577
